Democrats talk a lot about affordability. Could a message of prosperity be more powerful?

August 14, 2026

Listen and subscribe: Apple | Spotify | Wherever You Listen

Sign up to receive our twice-weekly News & Politics newsletter.

The Washington Roundtable’s Evan Osnos interviews the former Commerce Secretary and Rhode Island governor Gina Raimondo about a problem she’s been working on since she left the Biden Administration: how to make sure that the A.I. revolution does not leave American workers behind. Drawing on her father’s experience of losing his factory job in the wake of outsourcing to China, Raimondo warns against repeating the mistakes of the past and argues that the U.S. needs a plan to help workers navigate the A.I. transition. “We can’t put the toothpaste back in the bottle. A.I. is out there,” Raimondo says. “We want to harness the good, but be intentional about having a plan and safeguards for the bad.” She also discusses why Democrats should focus not just on affordability but on the politics and promise of prosperity and the American Dream.

华盛顿圆桌会议的埃文·奥斯诺斯采访了前商务部长、罗德岛州州长吉娜·雷蒙多，讨论了她离开拜登政府后一直在研究的一个问题：如何确保人工智能。 革命并没有让美国工人落后。 雷蒙多借鉴了她父亲在外包给中国后失去工厂工作的经历，警告不要重蹈过去的错误，并认为美国需要一项计划来帮助工人驾驭人工智能。 过渡。 “我们不能把牙膏放回瓶子里。 人工智能。 就在那里，”雷蒙多说。 “我们希望利用好的一面，但也要有意识地为坏的一面制定计划和保障措施。” 她还讨论了为什么民主党不仅应该关注负担能力，还应该关注政治以及繁荣和美国梦的承诺。
